neighbours.label: the opening piece of a split Greek- or Latin-derived technical word (immun|o-, imm|uno, ap|ol-, apo-, auto|ant-) before its stem; weaker on whole-token kin such as 'immune'
fire: Serum immunoglobulin levels fell sharply after the transplant.
The biopsy was stained by immunohistochemistry to locate the receptor.
Checkpoint immunotherapy has changed the outlook for melanoma.
An immunoassay detected the toxin at nanogram concentrations.
Her autoantibody titres rose before any symptoms appeared.
The gene encodes an apolipoprotein that carries cholesterol in the blood.
Sweat from apocrine glands has a stronger odour than eccrine sweat.
Early Roman emperors were granted apotheosis after death.
quiet: The vaccine gives lasting immunity against measles.
The hospital installed an autofocus camera in the operating theatre.
Preachers warned that the apocalypse was near.
The doctor ordered an autopsy the following morning.
An automatic door closed behind the surgeon.
The fans queued for a signed photo after the match.
The mitochondrial membrane folds inward into deep ridges.
The pharmacist checked the prescription twice before dispensing it.

predictions: fire 7-8 of 8 at 0.3-0.85; everyday whole-token auto-/apo- words (autopsy, apocalypse, automatic) under 0.05; 'immunity' may leak around 0.4 like 'immune' did
short: split Greek prefix piece (immuno-, apo-, auto-)
notes: Probe: ap|ol|ipoprotein 0.845, immun|odeficiencies 0.739, apo|theosis 0.741, imm|uno|affinity 0.640, auto|antibodies 0.354, immun|ocompromised 0.303; whole-token immune 0.453 (leak), Chlor|ophyll 0.403, apost|le 0.184, automatically 0.006.
